source.title: GNN-VPA: A Variance-Preserving Aggregation Strategy for Graph Neural Networks
source.authors: Lisa Schneckenreiter; Richard Freinschlag; Florian Sestak; J. Brandstetter; G. Klambauer; Andreas Mayr

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses signal-propagation theory to develop variance-preserving aggregation and reports how its method performs; it does not test the listed claim versions about training error, local minima, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy comparisons, but those do not measure training classification error. Its learning-curve results concern the paper's new aggregation method and convergence speed.
record.test_reason: The study uses signal-propagation theory to design graph aggregation and compares its method's performance. It changes aggregation, not initialization, depth, shortcuts, learning-rate stability or batch normalization. Its convergence results therefore do not test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that VPA retains SUM's expressive power and improves learning dynamics and predictive performance. Variance preservation is proved under simplifying distributional assumptions; all tested shallow networks trained without divergence, and benefits for very deep or normalization-free GNNs remain prospective.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a variance-preserving aggregation function for graph neural networks; it does not use the original claim's benchmark settings or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Aggregation choice (VPA versus SUM, MEAN, or MAX); social-dataset node-feature setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report faster GIN training-loss convergence with VPA than SUM across the displayed graph benchmarks. Aggregation changes in both message passing and graph-level readout; default hyperparameters favor SUM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variance-preserving aggregation can accelerate convergence relative to SUM in the tested five-layer GIN graph-classification settings.

record.problems: The learning-curve result is presented in a figure without numerical curve values. The authors note that GNNs in the tested datasets were shallow and all methods trained without divergence from exploding activations.
record.rows_left_out: Test-accuracy comparisons in Table 1 and Table B1 were left out because they do not measure the training-error behavior in the claim. No other training-curve conditions are shown beyond the nine datasets represented in Figure B1.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size, regularization and training-duration conditions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, special initialization of deep plain networks and Fixup residual training.

Effects of activation-matched initialization on training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and deep orthogonal convolution kernels. Initialization theory is assumed, without an initialization comparison.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training and divergence conditions.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The row states indicate inability to assess V1–V6, not absence of the reported convergence advantage. The supplied figure extraction lacks readable curve trajectories, so dataset-specific effect sizes and exceptions cannot be independently checked.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size and training-duration conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth-related training error and identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Training above the stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence conditions.
Batch-normalization effects on speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: GIN
rows.size_stated: 5 GNN layers; message dimension 64; classifier MLP hidden dimension 64
rows.operation_detail: Compared GIN training-loss curves using VPA versus SUM aggregation.
rows.note: The authors state that GIN training converges faster with VPA than SUM; the individual curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Valid aggregation-method comparison, but it measures no listed version. Faster convergence is stated in Appendix B.3; numerical curves cannot be verified from the supplied text.
